Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Since becoming a cultural phenomenon in the early 2000s, the Grand Theft Auto series has been one of the most popular gaming franchises in history. Naturally, this has attracted gamers of all ages looking to play each new entry, despite the fact that the series is clearly geared toward older audiences. With its sandbox open-world and high level of detail, many younger gamers around the globe are undoubtedly trying to convince their parents to let them play Grand Theft Auto 6 this week and be part of the conversation, in spite of its M rating.

If you're finding yourself in this situation within your own family, I can provide more context on just how mature GTA 6 really is, and whether or not you'll want to let a child under the age of 17 play it for themselves. While the ESRB already has a great write-up that explains many of the specifics for why GTA 6 has received a "Mature" rating to begin with, I've completed the game and will help provide additional color to just how much the game pushes the boundaries.

At first glance, the violence in Grand Theft Auto 6 might seem a bit reined in. This isn't like a Mortal Kombat or Gears of War game, where blood and guts are flying everywhere. Instead, GTA 6 is much more rooted in realism, which is reflected in its level of violence. People who are killed quickly fall to the ground, with those who merely get injured being left to writhe on the ground in pain.

While this might seem okay, I actually found the violence in GTA 6 a bit more bothersome at times because of how realistic it seemed. In my opinion, it's easy to write off games like Mortal Kombat that are so over-the-top with their own violence. For GTA 6 to reflect the real world a bit more makes its most brutal moments that much more gruesome.

And just because the gore in GTA 6 isn't as prominent as in other games doesn't mean that it's still not present. Body dismemberment can happen in GTA 6 , although the game does also give you the option to turn this off. Headshots with more powerful weapons can also result in some particularly nasty gore. Given that just about anyone in the world of GTA 6 can be killed at any point, whether by gun, vehicle, or other means, it can lead to the game being particularly brutal.

If you're worried about cursing in Grand Theft Auto 6 , well, there's no way to ignore it. Virtually every swear word you can think of is not only featured in GTA 6 , but they show up incredibly often. By my own estimation, I think I heard the F-bomb alone at least every 30-60 seconds, with certain cutscenes increasing this frequency drastically.

There are also occasional slurs used in GTA 6 as well. These words aren't used flippantly, as they're instead only said by some of the worst people you'll come across in the story of GTA 6 . Still, they're very much present in the game, which is worth keeping in mind.

Crude humor is also prominent throughout Grand Theft Auto 6's world of Leonida. GTA 6's TV channels and radio stations have no filter, with characters being able to say and show anything that they want. As a result, even if you're just driving around and listening to the radio, you never know when you might hear something that's quite vulgar in nature.

Sexual content in Grand Theft Auto 6 is likely where the game pushes things to the limit the most. Strip clubs from the franchise's history are once again present in GTA 6 , which is accompanied by plenty of nudity and raunchy imagery. Engaging with dancers at strip clubs is optional, but there are certain story missions throughout where you'll have to visit these locations no matter what.

Even outside of a sexual context, nudity is also rife throughout GTA 6 . Some of the nudity is played for laughs, but other instances of it, like with the nude beaches you can find, simply have NPCs laying it all bare for the heck of it. Even when characters aren't nude, there are also plenty of others you'll see running around the nude that are scantily clad.

Jason and Lucia, the two main characters in GTA 6 , can also develop a romantic relationship in the game. This leads to instances where players can prompt optional sexual encounters between the two. Not much is ever shown in these moments, as the camera often quickly cuts away, but there's still brief nudity for each shown in the scenes.

Drugs are featured early and often throughout Grand Theft Auto 6 . Not only do both Jason and Lucia smuggle and sell drugs in the game, but they are also given the option to partake in doing certain drugs themselves.

Even if you keep Jason and Lucia clean, there are countless other characters who are not like this. Cocaine is probably the most commonly seen drug throughout the game, but there are other harder drugs mentioned as well. Even though drugs are vital to GTA 6's story and the pursuit of earning money, they're also never glorified in the game, as those who do drugs are often looked down upon.

In short, Grand Theft Auto 6 is one of the more mature games I have played in a very, very long time. While many games have received M ratings for much less, GTA 6 feels like it's often pushing the boundaries of this rating.

As someone with kids myself, I can strongly urge that you don't allow them to play Grand Theft Auto 6 until they're older. Although I'm very much opposed to the notion that a game like GTA 6 would turn someone into a criminal themselves, there's still plenty of content within this game that is just not suited for tweens or younger teens. If GTA 6 is anything like its predecessor, it should remain relevant for the better part of the next decade, which means that those who might be too young to play it now should be able to do so at some point once they've aged up a bit.

articles.content:
If there was a Mt. Rushmore for hosts of food television shows, Gordon Ramsay is up there zero questions. As such, I tend to respect the things he says when it comes to the food world, but now I'm questioning the legend. This guy hates air fryers, and I can't help but feel he's being a bit pretentious.

I was willing to defend Ramsay after he dissed pineapple on pizza , as that's a pretty standard opinion to have. I even continue to tune into his shows, despite them largely feeling like the same show as the last one, with a slightly different name .

What I can't abide is the disrespect he showed toward the air fryer. His comments make it sound like it has no place in the standard home kitchen. As someone who cooks from home all the time, I can't praise the air fryer enough, and how it elevates my cooking experience each and every dinner night.

articles.title: Playbill Apologizes Over 'George Floyd Musical' Ad & Bans Producer From Listings; Show's Controversial Creator Previously Sued Off Broadway Venue Over BIPOC Nights

articles.content:
Playbill , the ubiquitous and indispensable New York-based theater publication that features show synopsis, cast biographies and, on its website, stage-related job listings, apologized today for one such ad: a listing calling for singers interested in auditioning for a new concept stage musical album.

The cast album's title: George Floyd: The Musical .

The so-far-unrecorded and unstaged project carries the tagline, "The $20 Bill That Changed the World!"

The offensive Playbill listing immediately drew comments that were both irate and baffled, including some from Broadway stars. "Wtf," commented Derek Klena. "Ummm….?," wrote Rachel Zegler. And Joy Woods, starring in the current Galileo , surmised the whole thing must be an AI joke. blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-article1-uid0' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article1","mid","mid-articleX","mid-article","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article") .addSize([[2,2],[300,250],[620,350],[300,251],[501,282],[3,3],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; }); Related Stories News Playwrights Horizons Sued Over Discount Tickets For BIPOC Audiences News Broadway's Playbill Joins Twitter Exodus Citing Platform's "Hate, Negativity, And Misinformation"

But it was no joke, at least not the type of joke most on Broadway would appreciate. The company that took out the ad is Busted Broadway , a recently founded New Jersey-based independent musical theater record label developing such projects as Human Centipede: The Musical and Genghis Khan: The Musical (selections from both available on YouTube) and George Floyd: The Musical , coming soon according to the label's website . Watch on Deadline if ( !window.pmc.harmony?.isEventAdScheduledTime() ) { pmcCnx.cmd.push(function() { pmcCnx({ settings: { plugins: { pmcAtlasMG: { iabPlcmt: 2, } } }, playerId: '32fe25c4-79aa-406a-af44-69b41e969e71', playlistId: '0199e506-e642-7728-8264-463efe71337b', }).render("connatix_contextual_player_div"); }); } else { // This should only be get called when page cache is not cleared and it's event time. window.pmc.harmony?.switchToHarmonyPlayer(); }

Floyd was the African American man murdered by a white police officer in Minneapolis, Minnesota, in 2020. Floyd had been identified by a store clerk as having passed a counterfeit $20 bill. One of the police officers who were detaining Floyd at the scene, Derek Chauvin, knelt on the suspect's neck and back, asphyxiating him despite the man's dying plea, "I can't breathe." The killing sparked nationwide protests; Chauvin was found guilty on three murder and manslaughter charges.

This week, outrage over the jobs listing in Playbill was swift. "This is in incredibly poor taste," a commenter wrote. "This isn’t edgy."

And: "Can anyone explain to me why 'George Floyd' and 'comedic Musical' are in the same sentence?? I actually want answers on why this is okay or appropriate???"

And: "I didn’t know systemic racism and violence was comedic." blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dl-mid-article-inject2-uid1' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-article2","mid-articleX","mid-article","mid","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-article2") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,350],[2,4],[4,2],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() .setClsOptimization("minsize") ; });

And: "Hell isn’t hot enough for yall cause a George Floyd musical, satire or not is in such disgustingly bad taste. For yall it might not matter but he still had a daughter, and a family that have to see yall turn his death into a joke."

And: "Hell is hot & ready for you. Weirdos making an injustice out to be musical. May you never rest."

And then: "Your day is coming."

The reader reaction was enough to push Playbill toward swift, or reasonably swift, action. On its Instagram page today, Playbill wrote: "Late yesterday afternoon, Playbill Jobs incorrectly approved a job listing that had no place on our site. Once leadership was alerted, the listing was immediately removed, and we began reviewing and revising our approval processes. We apologize unequivocally for giving this hateful listing any further air, and we promise to do better going forward. We at Playbill aim to lift up this community with empathy, consideration, and respect. We hope those who read and follow us do the same.

"We know this listing has upset and offended many," Playbill continued, "and the fact that it made it onto our site has disappointed those who trust us as an outlet. For that, we are sorry, and are committed to regaining your trust."

In a just-released statement posted to its social media pages, the record label says, "Busted Broadway seeks to push the limits of what is possible in musical theatre by producing provocative and satirical musical cast albums. Our George Floyd the Musical is NOT making light of, condoning, or mocking the horrific 2020 murder of George Floyd. It's a satire on the CULTURE, rather than the person. Never judge a show by its title, as many who have never seen the script or score appear to be doing now."

Busted Broadway is based in West Milford, New Jersey, and was founded last year, according to its website, "out of a necessity to reinvigorate the barren wasteland of mundane, mediocre musical theatre shows foisted upon audiences today."

The site states that the founders are "a small team of passionate musicians and artists devoted to the funny, absurd, and ridiculous humor baked into our collective human condition." Busted Broadway, the description continues, "is not for the mollycoddled or politically correct listener." The label "exists to shake the snow globe and remind audiences that laughing at dark humor is not only allowed but necessary."

Busted Broadway's mission statement is to create and develop streaming albums and videos "too ridiculous , too raunchy , and too absurd to see the stage…If you like twisted showtunes, dark comedy, and Broadway gone completely off the rails, you’re in the right place."

One of the label's founders and composers is Kevin Lynch , who, according to his bio , is a "Berklee-trained producer, composer, songwriter, and performer [who] has built a career on his tireless momentum—scoring films, directing musical productions, and collaborating with Broadway legends."

"Kevin’s boundless curiosity and innovative approach have established him as a sought-after creative partner, blending experience and intuition with seamless collaboration," the bio states.

Lynch, according to this website , was playing piano by ear at five years old, joined The Juilliard School as staff accompanist, and went on to serve as music director for venues including the Mayo Performing Arts Center, Centenary Stage Company, and Royal Caribbean Cruise Lines.

But until the George Floyd musical, Lynch was perhaps best known for the lawsuit he filed last year against the venerable Off Broadway company Playwrights Horizons condemning the venue's "BIPOC Night," in which patrons who identified as black, indigenous, or people of color were offered discount tickets to a performance of Nazareth Hassan's play Practice . (BIPOC nights had become increasingly common since Broadway's Slave Play used the approach to diversify audiences beyond theater's largely white, largely upper-income attendees.) blogherads.adq.push(function () { blogherads .defineSlot( 'medrec', 'gpt-dsk-tab-mid-articleX-uid2' ) .setTargeting( 'pos', ["mid-articleX","mid-article","btf","300x251"] ) .setTargeting( 'viewable', 'yes' ) .setSubAdUnitPath("ros\/mid-articleX") .addSize([[300,250],[300,251],[620,366]]) .exemptFromSleep() ; });

The lawsuit stated that "because [Lynch] is white, he paid full price. Many other patrons also paid full price for Practice . All are harmed by Playwrights’ discriminatory pricing, and all are entitled to recover."

The suit sought to represent all ticket buyers who allegedly paid more for tickets than the discounted amount. According to the suit, Lynch bought two tickets to Practice for $90 each. Patrons using the BIPOC night discount code paid $39 a ticket.

The suit was settled out of court last May, with Playwrights Horizons releasing a statement saying, “Playwrights Horizons regrets that Mr. Lynch felt excluded because of his race…Playwrights Horizons and Mr. Lynch have agreed to resolve the matter out of court."

In a statement to The New York Times delivered by his attorney after the undisclosed settlement was reached, Lynch indicated he was pleased with the outcome and noted, "Race-based ticket pricing violates all our civil rights, regardless of which race is on the receiving end of the discrimination. I consider it a victory for civil and human rights.”

Deadline has reached out to both Playbill and Busted Broadway for additional comment.

articles.title: One of Storm's Most Disturbing X-Men Stories Is Getting a Horrifying New Chapter in Midnight X-Men
articles.summary: Image Courtesy of Marvel Comics Midnight X-Men opened its first issue with the mutant vampires already in existence, and it showed that Storm might be the most powerful of them all. The second issue took a break to go back in time and show how this all started, and it looked very familiar. As expected, Storm showed herself to be […]

Share on X (Opens in new window) X Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) Facebook Add Us On Google Midnight X-Men opened its first issue with the mutant vampires already in existence, and it showed that Storm might be the most powerful of them all. The second issue took a break to go back in time and show how this all started, and it looked very familiar. As expected, Storm showed herself to be a powerful and very well-respected empyre, and the second issue showed that she was also where it all began. This book showed the origin story of the mutants becoming vampires, and Storm was the first of them all after Dracula convinced her to change and accept his invitation to turn willingly.

In Midnight X-Men #2 by Jonathan Hickman and Matteo Della Fonte, Dracula tempted Storm to change, and she accepted. Storm then set a trap to lure in the X-Men and helped Dracula change them all in the ultimate betrayal. This played into the first time that Storm met Dracula, and in that previous meeting, Storm refused his temptations.

Midnight X-Men #2 showed how this terrible timeline ended up creating a war between vampires, empyres, mutants, and humans. This all started when Dracula summoned Storm to him. He then explained his entire origin to her, including how his own master took his life when his master realized the weakness of seeing his own kind being hunted down and killed. However, in Storm, he saw that she was different, calling her the most powerful and mighty of all the mutants. He offered to give her eternity, and she agreed and gave herself over to him.

That led Storm to become the first empyre, and then she did the unthinkable. She called out for help, pulled in the X-Men, attacked them with Dracula, and turned them too. Dracula and Storm turned Iceman, Angel, Beast, and Jean Grey. Only Cyclops and Kitty Pryde escaped. After this, Jean Grey tricked Cyclops into returning with a new team to save her, and it was another trap, with Storm once again showing her place as the leader. By the end, Storm and her new empyres had turned or killed several mutants, and she was a genuine villain. While she seemed almost sympathetic when meeting with Nightcrawler in the first issue, she was corrupted here.

This calls back to a previous X-Men issue, the first time that Storm met Dracula. In The Uncanny X-Men #159 (1982), Storm was out walking alone in New York City when she was attacked by someone. She began to grow weak, and it was Kitty Pryde who realized that something was wrong with her and that it might tie into the legend of vampires. When Storm disappeared, Kitty Pryde told the X-Men that she believed Dracula was responsible, and the mutants learned it was true.

This led the X-Men to seek her out at Belvedere Castle, and they soon realized they couldn't match up to the legendary vampire. However, the setup here was hugely different from what happened in Midnight X-Men . The setup was different. In Midnight X-Men , Dracula lured Storm in and gave her the choice, although that is not to say that he wasn't using some of his vampire powers of hypnosis on the mutant. In this earlier story, he fed on her and tried to force her to become one of his brides against her will.

That was the main difference. When Kitty Pryde gave herself to Storm and said she was willing to die, that snapped Storm out of it. Dracula told Storm to slaughter her teammates in the X-Men, and she attacked Dracula instead. This led to a giant battle between her and Dracula, which ended with Dracula finally admitting he admired her standing up for herself, then leaving, while also declaring that they were enemies forever. It was a wild and different X-Men story for the time, and it clearly influenced the new Midnight X-Men comic series.

That story was also carried over to Mutant X by Howard Mackie and Tom Raney in 1998. That series was another multiversal story, this one with Havok ending up on a different Earth where Storm couldn't stop the transformation but remained a hero. She eventually killed Dracula in this timeline, and she kept working as a hero on a team called the Six, which showed that even as a vampire, Storm could be a hero. Midnight X-Men , though, showed the worst-case scenario, where Storm turned her own kind and helped slaughter those mutants not deemed worthy. This was a nightmare scenario of that classic X-Men storyline.

What are your thoughts on Midnight X-Men and making Storm its catalyst? Let us know how you think this storyline will end up in the comments below.

Davah Avena ( Firefly Lane, Zoey's Extraordinary Playlist ) will serve as writer and executive producer. Julianna LaRosa of ChangeUp Productions, Sofia Pernas and Sheree Guitar also exec producing.

Dr. Lucia follows the titular Lucia, a first-year resident at a prestigious Phoenix hospital whose life takes an unexpected turn following a near-death experience. Suddenly experiencing psychic visions, Lucia finds herself relying on extraordinary instincts that transform her approach to medicine and help her become the physician she's always aspired to be.
